text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty P1 fired: alert=CUDA_ALLOC_RETRIES spike in pool=gpu-pool-eu-west-1. Symptoms: repeated cuda kernel timeouts -> transient OOMs -> request failures. PD: https://pagerduty.com/incident/PD12345 
pagerduty: Incident created (PD12345). Urgency: high. Notifications sent to: @anya, @maria. 
anya (oncall): acked the page. I'm on it — pulling logs and checking pool health. 
anya (oncall): quick check: are we seeing core OOMs or allocation retries? grafana: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/allocs/gpu-allocs?orgId=1&var-pool=gpu-pool-eu-west-1 
maria (infra): I'm seeing repeated "CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS" and "cuMemAlloc retry" in node-gpu-07 and node-gpu-09 over the last 3m. Kernel driver logs show timeouts. 
josh (runtime): same on runtime side: KV-cache fills then cuda alloc fails when multiple long-seq requests come in. Hit rate correlated with large-context jobs. 
anya (oncall): customer impact: some text-generation requests returned 502/503 from router with backend error code 137. I see ~14 unique customer API keys affected in last 10m, highest qps drop 20%. 
alex (sre): adding context: we rolled a nvidia-driver security patch in eu-west-1 earlier today (rollout at 03:20 UTC). Could be related. 
maria (infra): action plan suggestion: 1) temporarily drain the two hot nodes (gpu-07, gpu-09) from serving 2) enable fallback routing to model-compact for long-seq requests 3) increase kv-cache eviction threshold. 
anya (oncall): agreed. I'll hand off to infra for node drain. @maria can you cordon + migrate? Also create short-lived routing rule. 
maria (infra): running commands now: 
```
kubectl cordon node-gpu-07 --context=prod-eu-west-1
kubectl drain node-gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30
kubectl cordon node-gpu-09 --context=prod-eu-west-1
kubectl drain node-gpu-09 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30
```
(Using rollout hooks to avoid evicting stateful KV pods) 
josh (runtime): configuring runtime fallback: reducing weight for model-large-v2 for eu-west routing. Command: 
```
rtroute set-weight --pool eu-west-1 --model model-large-v2=0.2,model-compact-v1=0.8 --reason "mitigation cuda alloc failures"
```
I've applied that and confirmed traffic shift ~80% to compact. 
anya (oncall): good. Can we confirm error rate drop? 
alex (sre): checking logs + metrics. Error spike peaked at 03:36 UTC; after route change and drains error rate down 65% in last 2m. Some residual allocation retries on nodes still finishing pod terminations. 
maria (infra): drain completed for node-gpu-07 at 03:40 UTC; node-gpu-09 still terminating pods (3 left). 
anya (oncall): customer comms: posting interim in status page: "We are investigating elevated GPU allocation failures affecting inference in eu-west-1; mitigation in progress. Some requests may see degraded performance or retries." 
josh (runtime): temporary config tweak: reduce max_sequence_length for model-large-v2 on eu-west to 4096 to reduce KV pressure. Applied via config service. 
maria (infra): found kernel ring buffer showing repeated "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 79" messages which map to GPU MMU faults after the driver patch. Opening infra incident ticket for rollback test. 
anya (oncall): escalation checklist: if drains + routing doesn't stabilize in 10m, we'll escalate to oncall+eng-runtime+drivers and consider rolling back today's driver patch in eu-west. 
pagerduty: Note: PD escalation timer set to 10 minutes. Next escalation to: eng-runtime oncall. 
anya (oncall): quick verification: sample customer logs show retries and a single client saw an in-flight decode canceled. No data exfiltration risk. Impact rated P1 due to availability. 
alex (sre): plan for rollback test: repro on a single spare node with today's driver + reproduce long-seq job that triggers alloc retry. If reproducible, revert driver. 
maria (infra): spun up spare node (node-gpu-spare-12) with pre-patch driver, ran benchmark, couldn't repro. Running same job on patched node now. 
josh (runtime): also enabling more aggressive KV cache eviction policy on the runtime side to reduce persistent allocations: 
```
PATCH /api/v1/runtime/config
{ "kv_cache": { "max_entries": 60000, "eviction_policy": "lru_aggressive" } }
```
Applied. 
anya (oncall): update: error rate continues to fall, customer retries successful. Still seeing a handful of allocation retries from a noisy tenant (api-key: r-XXXX). Recommend throttling that tenant temporarily. 
maria (infra): throttled tenant r-XXXX at the router. Throttling rule: rate-limit 10 rps. 
josh (runtime): confirm: once noisy tenant throttled, allocation failures drop to near zero. Looks like kernel bug + hammering workload combo. 
anya (oncall): status: mitigation in place. Next steps: 1) keep drains until kernel vendor confirms fix / we roll back 2) schedule driver rollback if vendor advises 3) follow up with affected customers with root cause once confirmed. 
alex (sre): creating follow-up Jira: RED-INF-4321 with timeline + artifacts. 
pagerduty: PD12345 updated: mitigation applied; awaiting vendor analysis. 
anya (oncall): I'm going to hand off to morning shift at 04:20 UTC. @alex will take lead for postmortem and vendor coordination. 
alex (sre): taking handoff. I'll keep PagerDuty status updated and start a post-incident ticket with initial RCA draft. 
maria (infra): leaving note: nodes cordoned and drained; not returning to pool until cleared. 
josh (runtime): tagging runtime config changes in changelog and setting monitoring alert for kv-cache evictions so we catch similar patterns earlier. 
anya (oncall): thanks everyone. closing active paging loop for now — I'll put an incident follow-up on the calendar for 09:00 UTC. :white_check_mark: 
incident-bot: PD12345 acknowledged by anya (oncall). Resolution: mitigated; monitoring.
